rows.L0_notes: The stem and crown remain legible, but the thin left tip turns sharply down-left from an almost horizontal crown, producing a visible terminal kink.
rows.L1_notes: The zero-child unit is connected and readable, but its short left tip reverses downward at the end of the crown instead of continuing the crown tangent.
rows.pair_notes: Both panels show the same terminal-direction reversal and neither has a meaningful visual advantage.

rows.L0_notes: The upright child merges through the top elbow before becoming distinct, leaving a congested junction; the terminal tip also turns abruptly down-left.
rows.L1_notes: The single child is visibly connected but is packed into the crown elbow and shares the turn before separating; the left terminal also hooks down-left.
rows.pair_notes: Both panels have a readable main stem but combine an elbow-packed child with the same kinked terminal closure.

rows.L0_notes: A thin child shadows the underside of the crown and disappears into the elbow, reading as a stray parallel hair rather than a branch; the left tip is also kinked downward.
rows.L1_notes: The up-right child separates cleanly from the primary and the hierarchy is clear, but the left terminal turns down against the crown direction.
rows.pair_notes: B is clearly better because its child reads as an attached shoot; A has a parallel hair under the crown.

rows.L0_notes: The upward child is distinct and naturally attached, but the left terminal makes a sharp down-left hook from the crown.
rows.L1_notes: The child and main sweep are coherent, yet the thin terminal changes direction abruptly downward at the left end.
rows.pair_notes: The panels are visually equivalent and share the same terminal-continuity failure.

rows.L0_notes: Two narrow children rise almost parallel from a very small crown interval, forming a comb-like hair cluster that competes with the main sweep; the left terminal itself is continuous.
rows.L1_notes: The two children have distinct directions but converge into essentially the same elbow point, producing a crowded three-way junction; the left terminal also hooks downward.
rows.pair_notes: Both fail, but B's splayed child directions remain more legible than A's tight pair of parallel hairs.

rows.L0_notes: The zero-child unit has a dominant continuous sweep, a smooth rounded turn, and a tapered up-left terminal that follows the crown direction.
rows.L1_notes: The main stem is readable, but the thin terminal doubles down-left from a crown that is traveling up-left, leaving a conspicuous hooked finish.
rows.pair_notes: A preserves tangent continuity through the terminal; B visibly reverses direction at the tip.

rows.L0_notes: The two right-facing children are separated by position and direction and remain subordinate to the primary, but the left terminal bends sharply down from the crown.
rows.L1_notes: The inner child runs back beneath and nearly parallel to the crown, creating a second hair-like contour and weakening the hierarchy; the terminal also hooks down-left.
rows.pair_notes: A's two shoots remain distinct and readable, whereas B introduces a crown-parallel inner hair.

rows.L0_notes: The two children are visibly attached at separated locations and splay in distinct directions, but the terminal turns down-left instead of closing the crown continuously.
rows.L1_notes: Both children concentrate at the crown elbow, making the fork visually congested and reducing positional rhythm; the thin terminal also hooks downward.
rows.pair_notes: A has clearer child spacing and hierarchy; B compresses both shoots into the elbow.

rows.L0_notes: The zero-child primary is dominant and connected, and its thin up-left taper continues the crown direction into a coherent terminal closure.
rows.L1_notes: The sweep is otherwise clear, but the short terminal curls down-left from the horizontal crown, creating a visible end kink.
rows.pair_notes: A closes along the crown tangent; B reverses downward at the terminal.

rows.L0_notes: The primary rises and turns in one readable sweep, with a thin up-left taper that extends the crown cleanly; the zero-child rhythm condition holds by construction.
rows.L1_notes: The zero-child sweep is legible, but its thin left tip drops down-left at a hard angle from the crown.
rows.pair_notes: B has a continuous terminal taper, while A ends in a downward hook.

rows.L0_notes: The child runs left just beneath and nearly parallel to the crown, resembling an extra hair rather than a distinct shoot; the primary terminal also hooks down-left.
rows.L1_notes: The up-right child is cleanly attached and subordinate to the main sweep, but the left terminal turns sharply downward from the crown.
rows.pair_notes: B's child reads as a branch; A's crown-parallel child reads as a stray hair.

rows.L0_notes: The main sweep remains dominant, the right child separates naturally at the elbow, and the thin up-left terminal completes the crown as one coherent growth unit.
rows.L1_notes: The right child is clearly attached and the hierarchy is readable, but the short left terminal drops down-left from the crown and breaks tangent continuity.
rows.pair_notes: The child structure is comparably clear, but only B preserves terminal direction and whole-unit continuity.
